# Lab machinery: the estimator of the course, the specification menu, its
# validation, and the helpers of Tasks 4 and 5 – try_spec(), my_experiments(),
# submit_exploration(), prereg(), run_spec() and report_result(). The same
# code as R/spec_tools.R of the downloadable workspace, apart from the tag of
# the class chart, which lasts for the browser session here. Every
# specification is fitted live; data/spec_curve.csv places it among the 64,
# and data/menu_options.csv gives the reason for every option that is not on
# the curve. Both arrive with the page through its `resources:` list.

# ============================================================================
# CONFIGURATION – the class chart and the course site
# ============================================================================
# The results Form that submit_exploration() and report_result() pre-fill: its
# ID and the entry codes of its seven fields. They belong to the Form that the
# cases of the course share, set up for the EU-frames case; a Form of its own
# replaces them here and nowhere else. The word in .case_word follows the tag
# in every label, so that the chart of this case reads only its own rows.
.form_id <- "1FAIpQLSezoAEOnZUfP4pkfN28_XtEBwSyc2RLsXB-h8RPSegF7_t76A"
.form_entry <- c(spec = "entry.832496914", b = "entry.1656311800", se = "entry.1337458262",
                 t = "entry.1940779437", df = "entry.1682711955", n = "entry.1586392724",
                 r = "entry.1660273001")
.case_word <- "housing"
.course_url <- "https://codemoreh.github.io/applied-replication"
# ============================================================================


# ---- The estimator -------------------------------------------------------------
# A verbatim copy of R/housing/_tools.R in the course repository, which builds
# the curve; the downloadable workspace carries the same copy in R/spec_tools.R.

# The fits use stats only (and dplyr for the rows), on purpose: the same code
# runs in the downloadable workspace and in webR on the browser lab, so all
# three give the same numbers. R/housing/check_parity.R in the course
# repository checks it against estimatr (HC2) and marginaleffects (average
# marginal effects).

# The options of the curve, in menu order. Anything else is refused by
# check_spec() with the reason recorded in data/menu_options.csv.
SPEC_AXES <- list(
  comparison = c("white", "nonhispanic"),
  population = c("replies", "all"),
  uncoded    = c("drop", "not_named"),
  model      = c("lpm", "logit"),
  adjust     = c("none", "email", "place", "place_ethnic")
)

# Covariates of each adjustment set; all are recorded before the emails went out.
ADJUST_TERMS <- list(
  none         = character(0),
  email        = "hard_email",
  place        = c("hard_email", "pop_third", "poverty_third"),
  place_ethnic = c("hard_email", "pop_third", "poverty_third", "black_third", "hispanic_third")
)

# The analysed rows and the outcome of one specification. Bounced emails never
# reached an official and are outside the experiment under every option.
spec_frame <- function(audit, comparison = "white", population = "replies", uncoded = "drop") {
  audit |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(reply),
                  .env$comparison == "nonhispanic" | group %in% c("white", "hispanic"),
                  .env$population == "all" | reply == 1) |>
    dplyr::mutate(
      hisp = as.integer(group == "hispanic"),
      y = dplyr::case_when(reply == 0 ~ 0,
                           is.na(named) & .env$uncoded == "not_named" ~ 0,
                           .default = named)
    ) |>
    dplyr::filter(!is.na(y))
}

# HC2 standard errors (Neyman-style for a randomised comparison), written out so
# that no package is needed in the browser.
vcov_hc2 <- function(fit) {
  x <- model.matrix(fit)
  e <- residuals(fit)
  h <- hat(qr(x), intercept = FALSE)
  bread <- solve(crossprod(x))
  meat <- crossprod(x * (e / sqrt(1 - h)))
  bread %*% meat %*% bread
}

# Average marginal effect of hisp in a logit, with a delta-method SE taken from
# a numerical gradient: the mean of p(hisp = 1) - p(hisp = 0) over the analysed rows.
ame_logit <- function(fit) {
  x1 <- model.matrix(fit)
  x0 <- x1
  x1[, "hisp"] <- 1  # r-style: keep – a model matrix, not a data frame
  x0[, "hisp"] <- 0  # r-style: keep – a model matrix, not a data frame
  ame <- \(beta) mean(plogis(x1 %*% beta) - plogis(x0 %*% beta))
  beta <- coef(fit)
  grad <- purrr::map_dbl(seq_along(beta), \(k) {
    step <- 1e-6 * max(1, abs(beta[k]))
    up <- beta
    dn <- beta
    up[k] <- up[k] + step
    dn[k] <- dn[k] - step
    (ame(up) - ame(dn)) / (2 * step)
  })
  list(est = ame(beta), se = sqrt(drop(t(grad) %*% vcov(fit) %*% grad)))
}

# The conversion rules of Multi100 (standard_correlation_coefficient.R): t with
# its df; z with the sample size standing in for the missing df; a chi-square
# read as the square of a z, so it carries no sign.
r_multi100 <- function(stat, stat_type, df, n) {
  dplyr::case_when(
    stat_type == "t" ~ stat / sqrt(stat^2 + df),
    stat_type == "z" ~ tanh(abs(stat) * sqrt(1 / (n - 3))) * sign(stat),
    stat_type == "chi2" ~ tanh(sqrt(abs(stat)) * sqrt(1 / (n - 3)))
  )
}

check_spec <- function(comparison, population, uncoded, model, adjust) {
  chosen <- list(comparison = comparison, population = population, uncoded = uncoded,
                 model = model, adjust = adjust)
  bad <- names(chosen)[!purrr::map2_lgl(chosen, SPEC_AXES[names(chosen)], \(v, ok) v %in% ok)]
  if (length(bad) > 0) {
    stop("Not on the curve: ", paste0(bad, " = '", unlist(chosen[bad]), "'", collapse = ", "),
         ". The options are listed in data/menu_options.csv.", call. = FALSE)
  }
  invisible(TRUE)
}

# One specification: estimate in percentage points (negative = Hispanic names
# greeted by name less often, the direction of the claim), its SE, the test of
# the model that the specification fits, and the partial correlation by the Multi100 rule.
fit_spec <- function(audit, comparison = "white", population = "replies", uncoded = "drop",
                     model = "lpm", adjust = "none") {
  check_spec(comparison, population, uncoded, model, adjust)
  terms <- ADJUST_TERMS[[adjust]]
  frame <- spec_frame(audit, comparison, population, uncoded) |>
    dplyr::filter(dplyr::if_all(dplyr::all_of(terms), \(x) !is.na(x)))
  rhs <- paste(c("hisp", terms), collapse = " + ")
  form <- stats::as.formula(paste("y ~", rhs))

  if (model == "lpm") {
    fit <- stats::lm(form, data = frame)
    coef_b <- unname(coef(fit)["hisp"])
    coef_se <- sqrt(vcov_hc2(fit)["hisp", "hisp"])
    stat <- coef_b / coef_se
    df <- fit$df.residual
    p <- 2 * stats::pt(-abs(stat), df)
    est <- coef_b
    est_se <- coef_se
    stat_type <- "t"
  } else {
    fit <- stats::glm(form, family = stats::binomial(), data = frame)
    coef_b <- unname(coef(fit)["hisp"])
    coef_se <- sqrt(vcov(fit)["hisp", "hisp"])
    stat <- coef_b / coef_se
    df <- NA_real_
    p <- 2 * stats::pnorm(-abs(stat))
    ame <- ame_logit(fit)
    est <- ame$est
    est_se <- ame$se
    stat_type <- "z"
  }

  n <- nrow(frame)
  data.frame(
    comparison = comparison, population = population, uncoded = uncoded,
    model = model, adjust = adjust,
    b_pp = 100 * est, se_pp = 100 * est_se,
    coef = coef_b, coef_se = coef_se,
    stat_type = stat_type, stat = stat, df = df, p = p,
    r = r_multi100(stat, stat_type, df, n),
    n = n, n_hisp = sum(frame$hisp == 1), n_comp = sum(frame$hisp == 0),
    rate_hisp = 100 * mean(frame$y[frame$hisp == 1]),
    rate_comp = 100 * mean(frame$y[frame$hisp == 0])
  )
}

# The free-text label that carries a specification to the class chart.
spec_line <- function(comparison, population, uncoded, model, adjust) {
  sprintf("comparison=%s population=%s uncoded=%s model=%s adjust=%s",
          comparison, population, uncoded, model, adjust)
}


# ---- The menu --------------------------------------------------------------------
# The eleven decisions in the order of the menu, each with the options that the
# curve keeps. The five decisions of SPEC_AXES keep two or more options, which
# multiply to the 64 specifications; on the other six the curve keeps one.
# Every other option is a row of data/menu_options.csv, whose reason the
# helpers print when it is asked for.
.menu <- list(
  # Level 1 – Estimands
  outcome    = "named",
  comparison = SPEC_AXES$comparison,
  population = SPEC_AXES$population,
  names      = "both",
  officials  = "any",
  # Level 2 – Measurement
  uncoded    = SPEC_AXES$uncoded,
  bounced    = "exclude",
  # Level 3 – Estimation
  model      = SPEC_AXES$model,
  adjust     = SPEC_AXES$adjust,
  inference  = "model",
  scale      = "pp"
)
.level_titles <- c(estimand    = "Level 1 – Estimands",
                   measurement = "Level 2 – Measurement",
                   estimation  = "Level 3 – Estimation")


# ---- The shipped files -----------------------------------------------------------
# Each file is read once and cached. The base reader keeps this code identical,
# line for line, with the copy in R/spec_tools.R of the workspace. An empty cell must read as
# NA, as readr reads it: the 14 authorities without community thirds would
# otherwise enter the adjusted models as a fourth level "".
.cache <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
.read_once <- function(name, path) {
  if (is.null(.cache[[name]])) {
    if (!file.exists(path))
      stop(sprintf("%s is missing – the page loads it through its resources list. Reload the page.",
                   path), call. = FALSE)
    assign(name, utils::read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, encoding = "UTF-8", # r-style: keep – the same reader as the workspace
                                 na.strings = c("", "NA")),
           envir = .cache)
  }
  .cache[[name]]
}
.audit   <- function() .read_once("audit", "data/housing_audit.csv")
.curve   <- function() .read_once("curve", "data/spec_curve.csv")
.options <- function() .read_once("options", "data/menu_options.csv")


# ---- Pages of the course site ----------------------------------------------------
.pages <- c(
  "cases/housing/index.qmd"       = "Case study",
  "cases/housing/menu.qmd"        = "Specification menu",
  "cases/housing/map.qmd"         = "Decision map",
  "cases/housing/multiverse.qmd"  = "Multiverse",
  "companion/experiments.qmd"     = "Audit experiments",
  "companion/binary-outcomes.qmd" = "Binary outcomes",
  "companion/dags.qmd"            = "Causal graphs and conditioning",
  "companion/multiverse.qmd"      = "The multiverse and its critics")
.page_ref <- function(path) {
  title <- if (path %in% names(.pages)) .pages[[path]] else path
  sprintf("%s, %s/%s", title, .course_url, sub("\\.qmd$", ".html", path))
}
.or_list <- function(x) {
  q <- paste0("\"", x, "\"")
  if (length(q) == 1) q else paste(paste(q[-length(q)], collapse = ", "), "or", q[length(q)])
}


# ---- Validation ------------------------------------------------------------------
# Two entry points into the same rules. .validate() takes a named list, which
# is how try_spec() supplies its arguments; .check_choices() reads the eleven
# my_* choices of the preregistration block. An option that is not on the
# curve stops with the reason from menu_options.csv, the page of the course
# site that teaches it, and the options that stay on the curve.
.on_menu <- function(axis, v) is.character(v) && length(v) == 1 && !is.na(v) && v %in% .menu[[axis]]

.refuse <- function(axis, v, as_args) {
  shown <- if (as_args) axis else paste0("my_", axis)
  keep  <- .menu[[axis]]
  map   <- paste0("  Every decision and its options: ", .page_ref("cases/housing/map.qmd"))
  if (!is.character(v) || length(v) != 1 || is.na(v))
    stop(sprintf("%s needs one option in quotes, for example %s = \"%s\".", shown, shown, keep[1]),
         call. = FALSE)
  opts <- .options()
  row  <- dplyr::filter(opts, .data$axis == .env$axis, .data$option == .env$v)
  off  <- dplyr::filter(opts, .data$axis == .env$axis, !.data$on_curve)$option
  msg <- if (nrow(row) == 1) c(
    sprintf("%s = \"%s\" (%s) is not on the curve of %d specifications, so it has no result here.",
            shown, v, row$label, nrow(.curve())),
    paste0("  Why: ", row$reason),
    paste0("  Where it is taught: ", .page_ref(row$taught_on)),
    map,
    sprintf("  To stay on the curve, choose %s = %s.", shown, .or_list(keep))
  ) else c(
    sprintf("%s = \"%s\" is not an option on the menu.", shown, v),
    sprintf("  On the curve: %s.", paste(keep, collapse = " | ")),
    if (length(off) > 0)
      sprintf("  Off the curve, refused with the reason why: %s.", paste(off, collapse = " | ")),
    map
  )
  stop(paste(msg, collapse = "\n"), call. = FALSE)
}

.validate <- function(ch, as_args = FALSE) {
  bad <- purrr::discard(names(.menu), \(a) .on_menu(a, ch[[a]]))
  if (length(bad) > 0) .refuse(bad[1], ch[[bad[1]]], as_args)
  ch[names(.menu)]
}

# The choices are looked up from the frame of this function outwards, which
# reaches the session in which the preregistration block was run.
.check_choices <- function() {
  need <- paste0("my_", names(.menu))
  ch <- mget(need, envir = environment(), inherits = TRUE, ifnotfound = list(NULL))
  missing <- need[purrr::map_lgl(ch, is.null)]
  if (length(missing) > 0)
    stop("Not declared yet: ", paste(missing, collapse = ", "),
         ". Fill in every choice in the preregistration block and run it first.", call. = FALSE)
  .validate(stats::setNames(ch, names(.menu)))
}


# ---- The live fit ----------------------------------------------------------------
# fit_spec() on the five decisions that vary on the curve, with the 95%
# interval of the estimate (t for the linear model, normal for the average
# marginal effect of the logit) and the place of the result among the 64. The
# fit is checked against its row of data/spec_curve.csv; a difference means
# that the page loaded an incomplete file.
.result <- function(ch) {
  fit <- fit_spec(.audit(), ch$comparison, ch$population, ch$uncoded, ch$model, ch$adjust) |>
    as.list()
  crit <- if (fit$stat_type == "t") stats::qt(0.975, fit$df) else stats::qnorm(0.975)
  curve <- .curve()
  stored <- dplyr::filter(curve, .data$comparison == ch$comparison, .data$population == ch$population,
                          .data$uncoded == ch$uncoded, .data$model == ch$model,
                          .data$adjust == ch$adjust)
  if (nrow(stored) != 1) {
    warning("This specification has no row in data/spec_curve.csv; reload the page.",
            call. = FALSE)
  } else if (abs(fit$b_pp - stored$b_pp) > 1e-6 || abs(fit$stat - stored$stat) > 1e-6) {
    warning(sprintf("The live fit (%.4f points, %s = %.4f) differs from the curve that this page loaded (%.4f points, %s = %.4f). Reload the page.",
                    fit$b_pp, fit$stat_type, fit$stat, stored$b_pp, fit$stat_type, stored$stat),
            call. = FALSE)
  }
  c(fit, list(ci_low = fit$b_pp - crit * fit$se_pp, ci_high = fit$b_pp + crit * fit$se_pp,
              further = sum(curve$b_pp < fit$b_pp - 1e-9), n_curve = nrow(curve)))
}


# ---- The printout ----------------------------------------------------------------
.comparison_label <- function(comparison)
  c(white = "white names", nonhispanic = "white and Black names")[[comparison]]

.fmt_p <- function(p) sprintf("= %s", format(signif(p, 2), scientific = FALSE))

.class_line <- function(res) {
  below <- res$b_pp < 0
  sig   <- res$p < 0.05
  if (below && sig) "below zero and significant at 5%, in the direction of the claim"
  else if (below) "below zero, but not significant at 5%"
  else if (sig) "above zero and significant at 5%, against the direction of the claim"
  else "above zero and not significant at 5%"
}

.print_result <- function(ch, res, lead = NULL) {
  unit <- if (ch$population == "all") "delivered emails" else "replies"
  test <- if (res$stat_type == "t") c(
    sprintf("  Test: t = %.2f on %d df, p %s (linear probability model, HC2 standard errors)",
            res$stat, round(res$df), .fmt_p(res$p))
  ) else c(
    sprintf("  Test: z = %.2f, p %s (logistic regression; the difference is its average marginal effect)",
            res$stat, .fmt_p(res$p)),
    sprintf("        logit coefficient %.3f, standard error %.3f", res$coef, res$coef_se)
  )
  writeLines(c(
    lead,
    paste0("  ", spec_line(ch$comparison, ch$population, ch$uncoded, ch$model, ch$adjust)),
    sprintf("  Greeted by name: Hispanic names %.1f%% of %d %s, %s %.1f%% of %d",
            res$rate_hisp, res$n_hisp, unit, .comparison_label(ch$comparison), res$rate_comp,
            res$n_comp),
    sprintf("  Difference: %.2f percentage points, 95%% interval %.2f to %.2f",
            res$b_pp, res$ci_low, res$ci_high),
    test,
    sprintf("  n = %d %s, partial r = %.3f (the conversion rule of Multi100)", res$n, unit, res$r),
    paste0("  Verdict: ", .class_line(res)),
    sprintf("  On the curve: %d of the %d specifications have an estimate further below zero",
            res$further, res$n_curve)))
  invisible(res)
}


# ---- Task 4: the exploratory helpers -----------------------------------------------
.tried <- new.env(parent = emptyenv())
assign("log", NULL, envir = .tried)
assign("last", NULL, envir = .tried)

# The first five arguments are the decisions on which the curve keeps more
# than one option; the other six are fixed on the curve, and asking for any
# other option of theirs prints the reason why it is not on the curve.
try_spec <- function(comparison = "white", population = "replies", uncoded = "drop",
                     model = "lpm", adjust = "none", outcome = "named", names = "both",
                     officials = "any", bounced = "exclude", inference = "model", scale = "pp") {
  ch <- .validate(list(outcome = outcome, comparison = comparison, population = population,
                       names = names, officials = officials, uncoded = uncoded,
                       bounced = bounced, model = model, adjust = adjust,
                       inference = inference, scale = scale), as_args = TRUE)
  res <- .result(ch)
  .print_result(ch, res, lead = "")
  row <- data.frame(ch, b_pp = res$b_pp, ci_low = res$ci_low, ci_high = res$ci_high,
                    stat_type = res$stat_type, stat = res$stat, p = res$p, n = res$n,
                    stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
  assign("log", dplyr::bind_rows(.tried$log, row), envir = .tried)
  assign("last", list(ch = ch, res = res), envir = .tried)
  invisible(row)
}

# The running log of everything try_spec() has fitted. Only the decisions that
# varied are shown; the others are those of the reference specification.
my_experiments <- function() {
  d <- .tried$log
  if (is.null(d)) {
    writeLines("Nothing tried yet – call try_spec() at least once.")
    return(invisible(NULL))
  }
  varied <- purrr::keep(names(.menu), \(a) dplyr::n_distinct(d[[a]]) > 1)
  show <- d |>
    dplyr::transmute(dplyr::across(dplyr::all_of(varied)),
                     estimate = round(.data$b_pp, 2),
                     interval = sprintf("%.1f to %.1f", .data$ci_low, .data$ci_high),
                     test = sprintf("%s = %.2f", .data$stat_type, .data$stat),
                     p = signif(.data$p, 2),
                     n = .data$n)
  writeLines(sprintf("Specifications you have tried (%d), estimates in percentage points:\n", nrow(d)))
  # wide enough for all five varied decisions on one line
  old_width <- options(width = max(getOption("width"), 120))
  on.exit(options(old_width))
  print(show, row.names = FALSE)
  writeLines(sprintf("\nEstimates from %.2f to %.2f points  |  below zero and significant at 5%%: %d of %d",
                     min(d$b_pp), max(d$b_pp), sum(d$b_pp < 0 & d$p < 0.05), nrow(d)))
  invisible(show)
}

submit_exploration <- function(nickname = NULL) {
  if (is.null(.tried$last))
    stop("Nothing to submit – call try_spec() first, ending with the specification you want on the chart.",
         call. = FALSE)
  .submit(.tried$last$ch, .tried$last$res, "explore",
          "Your exploratory submission (the last specification you tried):", nickname)
}


# ---- Task 5: the declared helpers --------------------------------------------------
# prereg() prints the block and returns it, so that run_spec() can check that
# the block has not changed since.
prereg <- function() {
  ch <- .check_choices()
  rows <- .options() |>
    dplyr::filter(paste(.data$axis, .data$option) %in% paste(names(ch), unlist(ch))) |>
    dplyr::arrange(match(.data$axis, names(.menu))) |>
    dplyr::mutate(line = sprintf("    %-31s : %-12s (%s)", .data$decision, .data$option, .data$label))
  block <- purrr::imap(.level_titles, \(title, lv) c(paste0("  ", title), rows$line[rows$level == lv])) |>
    unlist(use.names = FALSE)
  ph <- stats::setNames(rows$phrase, rows$axis)
  statement <- c(
    sprintf("%s%s, %s, %s, the difference in the share that drew %s between Hispanic names and %s (%s, %s).",
            toupper(substr(ph[["population"]], 1, 1)), substring(ph[["population"]], 2),
            ph[["names"]], ph[["officials"]], ph[["outcome"]], ph[["comparison"]],
            ph[["uncoded"]], ph[["bounced"]]),
    sprintf("Estimated with %s, %s, tested by %s and reported %s.",
            ph[["model"]], ph[["adjust"]], ph[["inference"]], ph[["scale"]]))
  writeLines(c(
    "DECLARED – your preregistered specification, fixed before it is fitted:",
    "",
    block,
    "",
    "  The estimand statement",
    strwrap(statement, width = 78, indent = 4, exdent = 4),
    "",
    "run_spec() and report_result() read these choices from here. Rendered into",
    "your report, this block is your preregistration, and it sits above the",
    "cells that fit and submit this specification."))
  invisible(structure(list(choices = ch), class = "housing_prereg"))
}

run_spec <- function(spec) {
  if (missing(spec) || !inherits(spec, "housing_prereg"))
    stop("Pass the object that prereg() returned: my_spec <- prereg(), then run_spec(my_spec).",
         call. = FALSE)
  if (!identical(spec$choices, .check_choices()))
    stop("The preregistration block has changed since prereg() returned this object. Run the whole block again, then run_spec(my_spec).",
         call. = FALSE)

## Task 2, continued – The estimand and the graph {#task-2-estimand-and-graph}

Before fitting anything, say what you are trying to estimate, in words. A template that you can adapt:

> The **unit-specific quantity** is, for each housing authority, the difference between whether it would come back with a reply that greets the sender by name to an email signed with a Hispanic name and to the same email signed with a white name. The **target population** is the public housing authorities that received an email.

There is a catch in that sentence. An authority whose official would not reply to one of the names has no greeting to compare. The comparison can then count every delivered email, a missing reply counting as no greeting, or count the replies only, which compares the authorities that replied to Hispanic names with those that replied to white names. These need not be the same authorities.

A causal graph makes the catch visible. A graph of this kind is a diagram of what causes what: variables are nodes, arrows run from cause to effect, and the rules for reading the graph say which paths between the name and the greeting are open, given what the comparison conditions on. The graph below is written in ordinary R, one arrow per string, each written the way it is drawn: `"name -> reply"` is the arrow from the name to the reply. The name can affect whether the official replies, and only a reply can greet the sender by name. Something about the official that nobody recorded (workload, habits of courtesy, attitudes) affects both whether they reply and how they greet, and so does the community of the housing authority. One arrow is switched off with a `#`: the arrow from the name to the greeting, which is the effect on tone that the claim is about.

.make_dag_builtin <- function(..., exposure, outcome, latent) {

.dag_has_edge <- function(dag, a, b) any(dag$edges$from == a & dag$edges$to == b)

# A node counts as one of its own descendants, which is what the collider rule
# below needs.
.dag_descendants <- function(dag, v) {
  kids <- setdiff(dag$edges$to[dag$edges$from %in% v], v)
  if (length(kids) == 0) v else .dag_descendants(dag, union(v, kids))
}

# Every simple path between two nodes, ignoring the direction of the arrows.
# The recursion is safe only because a teaching graph is tiny.
.dag_paths <- function(dag, from, to) {
  neighbours <- \(v) unique(c(dag$edges$to[dag$edges$from == v], dag$edges$from[dag$edges$to == v]))
  extend <- function(path) {
    v <- path[length(path)]
    if (v == to) return(list(path))
    purrr::list_flatten(purrr::map(setdiff(neighbours(v), path), \(w) extend(c(path, w))))
  }
  extend(from)
}

# A path is blocked by the set z if any node along it is either a non-collider
# inside z, or a collider with no descendant in z.
.dag_path_blocked <- function(dag, path, z) {
  if (length(path) < 3L) return(FALSE)
  purrr::some(seq(2L, length(path) - 1L), \(i) {
    node <- path[i]
    collider <- .dag_has_edge(dag, path[i - 1L], node) && .dag_has_edge(dag, path[i + 1L], node)
    if (collider) !any(.dag_descendants(dag, node) %in% z) else node %in% z
  })
}

# The backdoor criterion, brute-forced over subsets of the observed variables
# that are not descendants of the exposure: smallest sets first, and a set is
# skipped once it contains a set already found, which leaves the minimal ones.
.adjustment_sets_builtin <- function(x, exposure = x$exposure, outcome = x$outcome,
                                     effect = "total", ...) {
  if (!identical(effect, "total"))
    stop("The graph code built into this page answers the total effect only; paths() shows what a conditioning set opens and closes.",
         call. = FALSE)
  backdoor <- purrr::keep(.dag_paths(x, exposure, outcome), \(p) .dag_has_edge(x, p[2L], exposure))
  candidates <- setdiff(x$nodes, c(outcome, x$latent, .dag_descendants(x, exposure)))
  subsets <- c(list(character(0)),
               purrr::list_flatten(purrr::map(seq_along(candidates),
                                              \(k) utils::combn(candidates, k, simplify = FALSE))))
  closing <- purrr::keep(subsets, \(z) purrr::every(backdoor, \(p) .dag_path_blocked(x, p, z)))
  minimal <- purrr::reduce(closing, \(found, z)
    if (purrr::some(found, \(f) all(f %in% z))) found else c(found, list(sort(z))), .init = list())
  structure(minimal, class = "simple_dag_sets")
}

print.simple_dag_sets <- function(x, ...) {
  shown <- if (length(x) == 0) "(no set of observed variables closes every backdoor path)" else
    purrr::map_chr(x, \(z) if (length(z) > 0) paste0("{ ", paste(z, collapse = ", "), " }") else "{}")
  writeLines(shown)
  invisible(x)
}

# The paths between two nodes, each with its arrows, and whether it is open
# given the conditioning set Z; sorted as dagitty sorts them.
.paths_builtin <- function(x, from = x$exposure, to = x$outcome, Z = character(0), ...) {
  found <- .dag_paths(x, from, to)
  label <- purrr::map_chr(found, \(p) {
    steps <- purrr::map_chr(seq_len(length(p) - 1L),
                            \(i) if (.dag_has_edge(x, p[i], p[i + 1L])) " -> " else " <- ")
    paste0(p[1], paste0(steps, p[-1], collapse = ""))
  })
  open <- purrr::map_lgl(found, \(p) !.dag_path_blocked(x, p, Z))
  ord <- order(label, method = "radix")
  list(paths = label[ord], open = open[ord])
}

Now build the graph and put two questions to it. The first is what has to be adjusted for when the comparison counts every delivered email. The second is which paths from the name to the greeting are open once the comparison is made among replies only, which is what `Z = "reply"` asks: it conditions on the reply.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4.5
my_dag <- make_dag(
  # The name can affect whether the official replies at all.
  "name -> reply",
  # Only a reply can greet the sender by name.
  "reply -> greeting",
  # The official, whom nobody observed, affects both the reply and the greeting.
  "official -> reply",
  "official -> greeting",
  # So does the community of the housing authority, held in thirds in the data.
  "community -> reply",
  "community -> greeting",

  # The effect on tone that the claim is about: take the # off if you believe it.
  # "name -> greeting",

  exposure = "name", outcome = "greeting", latent = "official"
)

adjustmentSets(my_dag)
paths(my_dag, Z = "reply")
plot_dag(my_dag)
```
:::


`adjustmentSets()` returns `{}`, the empty set: nothing has to be adjusted for, because nothing points into the name. The names were assigned at random, so no common cause of the name and the greeting can exist. Conditioning on the reply changes the picture. The path through the reply closes, but two paths open, one through the community and one through the official, because the reply is a common effect of the name and of each of them (a collider), and comparing replies only conditions on it. This is the problem of conditioning on a consequence of the treatment, which @Coppock2019AvoidingPosttreatmentBias sets out for audit experiments.

Now take the `#` off the arrow `"name -> greeting"`, run the cell again, then run the cell below, which also adjusts for the community. Answer three questions for your own notes: why the adjustment set stays empty; which paths stay open among replies once the community is adjusted for, and what that means for a gap among replies; and which emails keep the comparison randomised.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
paths(my_dag, Z = c("reply", "community"))
```
:::


::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## Answers

1.  The set stays `{}` because nothing points into the name, whatever arrows leave it: the names were randomised.
2.  The direct path and the path through the official stay open. A gap among replies mixes the effect of the name on tone with differences between the officials who reply to each name, and adjusting for the community cannot remove the second, because the official is unobserved.
3.  Every delivered email, a missing reply counting as no greeting. That comparison estimates the effect of the name on receiving a greeting by name at all, which mixes the decision to reply with the tone of the reply.

The difference between the two comparisons is the decision on which emails are counted, the second argument of `try_spec()` in Task 4, and whatever you conclude here belongs in field 4 of your preregistration in Task 5.
:::

Now find out why it is 14.265. For a 2 × 2 table, `chisq.test()` applies the continuity correction of Yates unless it is told otherwise: it shrinks each gap between an observed and an expected count by 0.5 before squaring, a remedy designed for small tables. Preregistration means setting out your choice in a plan **before** you know what it does, which stops you from quietly picking the specification that happens to give the answer you wanted. ::: {.callout-important icon="false"}
## A shortened preregistration

*Each numbered comment maps to a question in the OSF "Preregistration Template from AsPredicted.org" (the eight-question short form). Because you are reanalysing data that already exist, field 2 also stands in for the prior-knowledge section of the secondary-data template (van den Akker et al. 2021) – the part that AsPredicted leaves out.*
:::

Make one choice on each decision of the [specification menu](menu.qmd), complete the dotted lines, then run the cell. The five decisions at Level 1 fix the question that you are asking, the two at Level 2 fix how the outcome is measured, and the four at Level 3 fix how it is estimated. The curve of 64 specifications keeps two or more options on five of these decisions and a single option on the other six. An option that is not on the curve stops `prereg()` with the reason why, as it stops `try_spec()`.


::: {.cell autorun='false'}
```{webr}
#| autorun: false
# ============================================================================
# MY PREREGISTRATION – one specification, declared before seeing its result
# ============================================================================
# 1. The claim I am testing: .................................................
# 2. The data + what I already know: housing_audit.csv (1,014 emails, public,
#    CC0); I know that the reference specification gives -19.97 points, and
#    what my exploration in Task 4 showed.
# 3. My one specification – one choice on each decision. An option that is
#    not on the curve of 64 stops prereg() with the reason why.

# Level 1 – Estimands (each of these changes what is being estimated)
my_outcome    <- "named"     # named   (greeted by name, the outcome of the claim)
my_comparison <- "white"     # white | nonhispanic   (white names, or white and Black names)
my_population <- "replies"   # replies | all   (replies only, or every delivered email)
my_names      <- "both"      # both   (male and female names pooled)
my_officials  <- "any"       # any    (replies from every official)

# Level 2 – Measurement (the same question, put to the data differently)
my_uncoded    <- "drop"      # drop | not_named   (the five replies without a greeting code)
my_bounced    <- "exclude"   # exclude   (the 23 emails that never arrived)

# Level 3 – Estimation (the same question and measures, another fit)
my_model      <- "lpm"       # lpm | logit   (difference in proportions, or logistic regression)
my_adjust     <- "none"      # none | email | place | place_ethnic
my_inference  <- "model"     # model   (HC2 t test, or the z test of the logit)
my_scale      <- "pp"        # pp   (percentage points)

# 4. Why this specification answers the claim, in one sentence grounded in
#    the causal graph of Task 2: .............................................
# 5. Supported if the estimate is below zero with p < .05 under the test of
#    the model; undermined if it is not significant or above zero. I will
#    report what I get.

my_spec <- prereg()   # checks every choice, prints your preregistration and keeps it
```
